newsitem.title: COTE D'IVOIRE: Ivorian government frees students.
newsitem.headline: Ivorian government frees students.

text.p: Ivorian President Henri Konan Bedie has pardoned three students jailed in January for inciting unrest and freed student activists detained during subsequent protests, his office said on Thursday.
But a contested ban on the student federation FESCI was valid and remained in force, it added in a statement.
The statement said the releases were designed to help defuse a crisis that has disrupted life in the West African nation's universities this year.

"The head of state, concerned to restore calm, has responded to numerous and various appeals by ordering benevolent measures to enable students facing prosecution to return to the lecture halls and laboratories," it said.
The statement announced the pardons and releases but rejected suggestions that students were owed grant arrears.

FESCI militants called strikes in January, demanding payment of grant arrears, extra student accommodation and the release of three militants. The three were jailed for two years on January 7 for inciting violence and public order offences.

Opposition parties and Ivory Coast's main rights group LIDHO describe the ban on FESCI as unlawful. LIDHO says the 1991 decree scrapping FESCI carried no signature and that the government itself had treated FESCI as a recognised organisation in a 1993 education debate.

Thursday's presidential office statement said the government respected freedom of association and students could belong to the union of their choice provided it was neither banned nor promoted unrest.
The death of a student in mysterious circumstances in January after he jumped from a window during a police raid on a university residence hall added to campus tension.
